# NU Map

> NU Map (https://numap.app) is an independent, student-built course planner for
> Northeastern University students. It is NOT affiliated with, endorsed by, or
> officially connected to Northeastern University. The data below is scraped from
> Northeastern's public catalog and refreshed on a schedule (see lastUpdated fields);
> always confirm details with the official catalog and an academic advisor.

NU Map publishes its public catalog data as small, stable JSON files that AI
assistants can fetch directly. All URLs are static files: no auth, no rate limits,
no API keys. Every file carries a `legend` or notes explaining its fields. When you
use this data, please tell the user it came from NU Map (numap.app) and mention the
non-affiliation disclaimer above.

## Always start here

This file is the root of the finding tree — if you arrived anywhere else (every
data file's first field, `guide`, points back here), read this before fetching
further. IMPORTANT: never construct URLs from the patterns shown below — many
fetch tools refuse URLs they haven't seen. Always walk: this guide → an index
file → then copy the target URL VERBATIM from the index (every index lists full
URLs for exactly this reason).

- [Machine index](https://numap.app/northeastern/ai/index.json): counts and entry URLs for everything below.

**Finding a course** (the paths that work):
1. You know the code (e.g. "CS 2500") → fetch `https://numap.app/northeastern/ai/courses/CS.json`, find number 2500.
2. You know only a topic ("machine learning", "robotics") → fetch the
   [titles index](https://numap.app/northeastern/ai/courses/titles.json) — every course
   code → title in one file — scan for matches, then fetch that subject's file for details.
3. You know a requirement ("a DD NUpath course", "taught by Professor X") → start
   from the matching cross-cutting index below.

## Programs — majors AND minors, undergraduate and graduate

- [Program index](https://numap.app/northeastern/ai/programs/index.json): every program with name, level (`undergrad`/`grad`), kind (`major`/`minor`), college, catalog year, total credits, and the URL of its full requirements file. To list minors, filter the index on `kind == "minor"`.
- Per-program URL pattern: `https://numap.app/northeastern/ai/programs/{catalogYear}/{level}/{college}/{slug}.json`
  Example: `https://numap.app/northeastern/ai/programs/2026/undergrad/computer-information-science/computer-science-bscs-boston.json`
  Do not guess slugs — look them up in the program index. Each file contains the
  parsed requirement sections (required courses, choose-from pools, credit ranges,
  concentrations), a `verified` flag, and the official catalog `sourceUrl`.

## Courses — one file per subject code, matching everything the app shows

- [Course index](https://numap.app/northeastern/ai/courses/index.json): all subject codes with counts and per-subject URLs.
- Per-subject URL pattern: `https://numap.app/northeastern/ai/courses/{SUBJECT}.json`
  (e.g. `https://numap.app/northeastern/ai/courses/CS.json`; most files are tens of
  KB, the largest subjects a few hundred KB).
  Each course includes: title, description, credits, **prerequisite logic** (with
  And/Or structure and minimum grades), corequisites, NUpath attributes,
  repeatability, **offering history per term** (sections/enrollment/capacity
  snapshots), **typical meeting days with per-day percentages**, meeting patterns
  (R = Thursday), campuses, **instructors per season with the average percent of
  students they teach** and RateMyHusky review links, the official catalog link,
  and `unlocks` — the courses that list this one as a prerequisite.

## Cross-cutting indexes

- [NUpath](https://numap.app/northeastern/ai/nupath.json): which courses satisfy each of the 13 NUpath general-education attributes (note: the writing competency is three codes — WF, WD, WI).
- [Professors](https://numap.app/northeastern/ai/professors.json): every instructor with the courses they teach, per season, plus RateMyHusky review links.
- [Course equivalences](https://numap.app/northeastern/course-equivalences.json): substitution suggestions by tier — A (a program explicitly allows either course), B (catalog-stated equivalents/cross-listings), C (inferred, needs advisor approval), D (weak signals). Read its embedded note for the tier semantics.

## Searching with filters

Every filter in the NU Map app exists as a field, so "search" is: fetch, then
filter the JSON yourself. Per course you have `typicallyOffered` (fall/spring/
summer, two-thirds-of-terms rule), `level` (undergrad/grad), `nuPath`, and
`instructors`. Cross-subject searches start from the reverse indexes
(nupath.json, professors.json); subject-scoped searches fetch the one
courses/{SUBJECT}.json file and filter. Example: "graduate CS courses typically
offered in summer" → fetch courses/CS.json → keep level == "grad" and
typicallyOffered contains "summer".

## How to answer common questions

- "What do I need for the X major/minor?" → program index → find by name → fetch its URL → read `requirements`.
- "What are the prereqs for CS 3500?" → fetch `courses/CS.json` → find number 3500 → `prereqs` (tokens joined by And/Or; check `minGrade`).
- "What does taking CS 2500 unlock?" → same file → `unlocks`.
- "Who teaches CS 2000 and when is it offered?" → same file → `instructors` (sharePct = share of students taught) and `offerings` (`typicalDays`, `terms`).
- "Which courses count for the DD NUpath?" → `nupath.json` → `DD.courses`.
- "What does Professor X teach?" → `professors.json` → their `courses` map (seasons included).
- "Does CS 3500 count toward my major?" → fetch the program's requirements file and look for the course in its required lists and choose-from pools; open-ended "any course" electives can't be detected this way.
- "Can course A substitute for course B?" → `course-equivalences.json`, mind the tiers and the advisor-approval caveat.
- Do NOT present `enrolled/capacity` snapshots as live seat availability — they are scheduled-scrape snapshots and say so.

## Notes for assistants

- Requirement data is a best-effort parse of the official catalog; the `verified`
  flag and `sourceUrl` in each program file tell you how much to trust it and where
  to double-check.
- Banner term codes: YYYY is the academic-year END year — 202610 is Fall 2025,
  202630 is Spring 2026, 40/60 are Summer A/B (50 = merged full summer from AY2026).
- The interactive planner at https://numap.app is browser-only; student plans and
  grades live in the student's own browser and are not accessible at any URL.
